requirement.part: cantilever bracket, load at the tip

reasoning: The load rose from 2500 N to 2800 N and REQ-006 adds a +10% load and -0.5 mm plate robustness check, so earlier designs must be rechecked. Ti-6Al-4V 12.5 x 25 mm is the only verified passing design at 194 g, so the Ti search should focus on the 12-13 mm width and 20-25 mm stock thickness range. Steel 4130 passes at 343 g, so its search should stay near 12.5-13 x 25 mm and avoid the failed 17.5 x 20 and 28 x 16 designs. No Al 6061-T6 design has passed REQ-006, and its low stiffness makes deflection the binding constraint, so its search should target thicker, narrower sections.

notes.Al 6061-T6: Search thicker sections (roughly 20-30 mm thick, 10-20 mm wide) because the 50 x 16 mm case fails REQ-003 at +10% load with 2.64 mm deflection against the 3 mm limit, and E = 68.9 GPa makes stiffness the binding constraint. Its 2700 kg/m3 density only pays off if the section stays compact, so check whether any stock thickness keeps mass below the 194 g Ti benchmark.
notes.Ti-6Al-4V: Search 12-13 mm width and 20-25 mm thickness around the verified 12.5 x 25 mm design (194 g), since 12 x 20 and 12.5 x 20 fail deflection at +10% load (3.34 and 3.21 mm). Only stock thicknesses 20 and 25 mm are valid, so test 12, 12.5 and 13 mm widths at 25 mm and reject any section with thickness/width above 2.
notes.Steel 4130: Search 12-13 mm width at 25 mm thickness, where 12.5 x 25 mm (343 g) and 13 x 25 mm (357 g) pass, because the 17.5 x 20 and 28 x 16 mm designs fail REQ-006 with MS -0.10. Steel's 7850 kg/m3 density means it is unlikely to beat the Ti benchmark, so keep it as a fallback and try 11-12 mm widths at 25 mm thickness only if they still meet REQ-007.

attacks.title: Heavier payload (+25%, 3500 N)
attacks.rationale: Stress test shows deflection rises to 3.126 mm, exceeding the 3 mm limit (REQ-003). Strength still passes (yield MS 0.293, ultimate MS 0.091). Deflection scales linearly with load, so stiffness headroom is only about +20% in load.

attacks.title: Longer arm (+10 mm, 150 mm)
attacks.rationale: Stress test shows deflection reaches 3.076 mm, exceeding the 3 mm limit (REQ-003). Deflection scales with length cubed, so the arm can grow only about 6% (to roughly 149 mm) before REQ-003 fails.

attacks.title: REQ-006 combined case (+10% load, 0.5 mm thinner plate)
attacks.rationale: Passes, but barely: yield MS 0.397, ultimate MS 0.178, deflection 2.968 mm against 3.0 mm. The 19.5 mm thickness is not a stock size (REQ-005), and the next stock size down (16 mm) fails by hand calculation (ultimate MS about -0.13, deflection about 4.9 mm). Width also has almost no slack: about 13.4 mm is needed for REQ-003 under this case, versus 13.5 mm in the design.

attacks.title: Machining loss (1 mm thickness)
attacks.rationale: Passes: deflection 2.917 mm, yield MS 0.459, ultimate MS 0.230. Headroom is small: thickness can lose only about 1.2 mm (minimum about 18.8 mm) before deflection exceeds 3 mm. Assumes tight machining tolerance.

attacks.title: Machining loss (1.5 mm width, to 12 mm)
attacks.rationale: Passes: deflection 2.813 mm, yield MS 0.437, ultimate MS 0.212. Width can lose only about 2.25 mm (minimum about 11.25 mm) before deflection exceeds 3 mm. REQ-004 floors width at 10 mm, and REQ-007 (thickness/width <= 2) would fail at 10 mm with 20 mm thickness.

summary: The Ti-6Al-4V 13.5 x 20 mm bracket passes all six structural and stability rules (S-01 to S-06) and the manufacturing and feasibility checks (M-02 to M-04, F-01 to F-03), with M-06 recorded as info for AMS 4911 annealed plate. Seven rules remain at action status (M-01, M-05, X-01, X-02, P-01, P-02, P-03), and P-04 is info only, so the design is not yet ready for release.
top_risks: X-02: Fatigue is not analyzed, and cyclic load cases such as launch vibration are still needed, so the passing structural margins (S-01 to S-03) do not yet cover fatigue life.

M-01: The design uses typical handbook allowables rather than MMPDS A- or B-basis values for this alloy, temper and thickness, so the margins in S-01 to S-03 may change when the correct allowables are applied.
X-01: The fracture control classification has not been assigned, which leaves the required fracture control rigor and rationale unrecorded.

actions.action: Replace the typical values with MMPDS A- or B-basis allowables for Ti-6Al-4V, the AMS 4911 annealed plate temper and the 20 mm thickness, then rerun S-01 to S-03.
Define cyclic load cases, including launch vibration, and complete a fatigue analysis for the bracket.
Classify the part (for example, non-fracture-critical) per NASA-STD-5019 and record the rationale in the compliance file.
Specify fastener material and finish at the joint to avoid galvanic corrosion per MIL-STD-889.
Require a certificate of conformance and mill test report traceable to the heat lot in the purchase order.
